_comment: One entry per lookup the agent can perform. Each becomes a separate
ElevenLabs webhook tool with its SQL pinned as a constant -- the model
supplies only the lookup value, bound as a query parameter.
match: 'exact' (default) keys off an id column; 'contains' does a
case-insensitive LIKE search, for when the caller knows a name but not a key.
latest_week_column pins a weekly-snapshot table to its newest period so a
search returns each product once instead of once per week.
Keep `description` sharply distinct between tools, including what each is
NOT for. gemma4-26b picks the tool from these words alone, and a small
model confuses overlapping descriptions.
Keep `columns` and `limit` small. Every value becomes words spoken aloud.
`subject` and `sample_questions` are shown to the person using the web UI, so they know what this agent can answer. They are not sent to the model.
`tables` describes each table for the person using the web UI: what it holds, its grain, and what it cannot answer. Shown in the guide, never sent to the model.
ADDING A TABLE -- four things must move together, or the agent and the
guide start describing different products:
1. Add the tool here, with `subject` and `sample_questions` so the web
guide has something to show.
2. Add the table to the `tables` block above: what it holds, its grain,
and what it cannot answer.
3. Re-read agent_prompt.md under 'What the data cannot tell you'. A new
table can make a stated limit obsolete, and the agent will keep
refusing questions it can now answer. Also check agent_greeting.txt,
which names what the agent handles. Then:
python configure_prompt.py --apply
4. If guardrails are enabled, re-read any custom guardrail that repeats
one of those limits in its own words.
Run `python databricks_tool.py --sync` after editing this file. It ends
with --check, which catches 1 and 2 and reminds you about 3 and 4.

ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_customers.label: Customer directory
ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_customers.about: Every active account: name, city, county, post code, the rep who owns it, delivery days and whether an appointment is needed. This is how a store name spoken out loud becomes an account key.
ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_customers.not_covered: Store names repeat -- many accounts share one, and some names cover twenty-odd different stores. A name alone never identifies an account; the city and the owning rep are what separate them.

ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_ac.label: Account activity and who to call
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_ac.about: One row per rep-and-account: when they last ordered, how long it has been, orders and order value recently and all time, their delivery days, and whether the account is flagged for attention and why.
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_ac.grain: current, stamped with the day it was built
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_ac.not_covered: Built from orders submitted through the app, so an account that orders by phone or email can look quiet when it is not. It also holds no invoices, returns, balances or credit terms, and nothing about which items an account buys.

ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.label: How a rep is doing
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.about: A rep's current month: orders submitted, total and average order value, their largest order, how many accounts ordered, a projection of where the month lands at this pace, and the same figures for the month before.
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.grain: current month per rep, stamped with the day it was built
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.not_covered: There is no target to compare against, so it cannot say whether a rep will hit their number. No margin, no branded share, no commission. These are orders submitted, not invoiced sales, and the two never tie out exactly.

ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_items.label: Product catalogue
ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_items.about: Every sellable product: name, category, price, case size, what is on hand and shippable, and whether it is on promotion, new, popular or discontinued.
ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_items.grain: one row per product; stock is last night's warehouse snapshot
ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_items.not_covered: Stock covers the warehouses the WMS mirror reaches, so an unknown stock figure means we cannot see it, not that the item is out. Product names are abbreviated, so search by a couple of plain words rather than an exact name.

ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.label: What an account was invoiced
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.about: One row per account per period: invoices, invoice value, average invoice, what came back as returns and whether returns are running over threshold, against the period before.
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.grain: current month per account, stamped with the day it was built
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.not_covered: Invoice values only exist from late September 2026 onward -- earlier invoices were exported without amounts and never will be. Each row carries a coverage figure saying how much of it is actually priced, and most accounts are still mostly unpriced. Counts and dates are complete.

ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.label: What an account buys
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.about: One row per account and item: how many times they have bought it, when they last did, the account's own typical gap between purchases, whether they are due or overdue, and whether they appear to have stopped.
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.not_covered: Due and overdue are judged against that account's own rhythm, not a company threshold, so a quarterly buyer is not overdue after a month. Value is subject to the same late-2026 pricing gap as invoices.

ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.label: What to pitch an account
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.about: A ranked list of items to raise with an account, each carrying the reason it made the list -- due to reorder, stopped buying, on promotion, peers buy it, or new and featured -- and the evidence behind it, with stock and promotion terms.
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.grain: ranked per account, rebuilt with the pipeline
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_accoun.not_covered: Only some reasons rest on the account's own buying; the rest are suggestions and must be spoken as such. An account with no purchase history gets a list made entirely of new and featured items, which is a weak list, not a strong one.

ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_ne.label: Accounts near an account
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_ne.about: For an account a rep is standing at, the nearby accounts within a few kilometres, ranked by urgency then distance, with why each needs attention.
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_ne.not_covered: Only accounts with coordinates appear, and distance is straight-line rather than driving. An isolated account will have no neighbours at all, which is not a failure.

ust_databricks.ust_facts.fct_orders.label: Orders as submitted
ust_databricks.ust_facts.fct_orders.about: Every order a rep submitted through the app: the account it was for, its value, how many items were on it, which channel it came through and the day it went in.
ust_databricks.ust_facts.fct_orders.grain: one row per order, same day
ust_databricks.ust_facts.fct_orders.not_covered: Only orders placed through the app. An account that phones or emails its orders does not appear here, and these are orders as submitted rather than what was finally invoiced, so they will not tie out with invoice figures.

ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.label: What a month was made of
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.about: A rep's invoiced month broken down: lines, distinct items and categories, the share that were promotional or new items, and the rate at which lines came back.
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.grain: current month per rep, stamped with the day it was built
ust_databricks.ust_reporting.mart_rep_pe.not_covered: Share of lines is sound; share of value rests on the same late-2026 pricing gap as everything else, and across the reps only about fifteen percent of lines are priced, so read the coverage figure before quoting a value share. There is no branded share here -- that needs a table that has not landed.

tools.name: lookup_rep_month
tools.description: How ONE REP is doing this month, by their name. Use for a rep asking about their own performance -- orders submitted, total and average order value, their biggest order, how many accounts ordered, where they are on pace to land by month end, and how that compares with last month. This is the rep's own numbers, not one account's: for a single store use lookup_account_status.
tools.subject: How am I doing?
sample_questions: How am I doing this month?
How does that compare to last month?
Where will I land by month end?
tools.answer_example: A hundred and fifty-six orders so far this month, about two million dollars, across seventy-seven accounts. At this pace you land near two point seven.

tools.name: lookup_biggest_orders
tools.from: ust_databricks.ust_facts.fct_orders o JOIN ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_customers c ON o.customer_key = c.customer_key JOIN ust_databricks.ust_dims.dim_reps r ON o.sales_code = r.sales_code
tools.description: ONE REP's biggest orders this month, largest first, each WITH THE CUSTOMER that placed it, how many items were on it, which channel it came through and the date. Use when a rep asks about their biggest or largest order, who it was from, or how their orders split across channels. Requires the rep's name. For their month as a whole -- totals, averages, pace -- use lookup_rep_month.
tools.subject: How am I doing?
sample_questions: What is my largest order and which customer?
Which of my orders came through the app?
tools.answer_example: Your biggest was fifty nine thousand three hundred and thirty four dollars, from Asian Food Store in Appleton, four hundred and ninety seven items, through the PDA on the second.

tools.name: lookup_rep_month_mix
tools.value_label: rep whose mix to break down
tools.description: What ONE REP's month was MADE OF: how many invoice lines and distinct items and categories, and the share of LINES that were promotional or new items, plus the rate at which lines came back. Shares here are by line, not by value -- too little of the invoice history carries a price for a value share to mean anything, so if someone asks for the split by value, say it is by line and that value coverage is too thin to divide up. These are invoiced lines, not orders submitted: for order counts, totals and pace use lookup_rep_month, and for individual orders use lookup_biggest_orders.
tools.subject: How am I doing?
sample_questions: What was my month made of?
How much of my month was promo or new items?
tools.answer_example: Two thousand and ninety-eight lines across thirteen hundred items and ten categories. Promotions were about four percent of lines, new items about six.

tools.name: lookup_account_invoiced
tools.description: What ONE account was actually INVOICED this month, and what came back as returns. Use for what a store really bought, their invoice value, how it compares with last month, and whether returns are running high. This is posted invoices, which is different from orders submitted -- for order activity and when they last ordered use lookup_account_status instead.
tools.subject: How am I doing?
sample_questions: What did Red Apple Market buy last month?
How are returns looking for that account?
tools.answer_example: Five invoices this month. Only part of that is priced in our data, so I can give you the count with confidence but not the full value.

tools.name: lookup_account_top_items
tools.description: What ONE account actually buys, item by item, most often first. Use for what a store orders, how often they take it, and when they last did. This is their purchase history -- for what to PITCH them next use lookup_pitch_list, which ranks by opportunity rather than by how often they have bought.
tools.subject: What should I sell them?
sample_questions: What does Red Apple Market usually buy?
What are their top items?
tools.answer_example: They buy KYJ Pork Sausage most often — five hundred and ninety-five times, last on the eleventh of August.

tools.name: lookup_pitch_list
tools.description: What to walk in and TALK ABOUT with ONE account: items ranked by opportunity, each with the reason it made the list and the evidence behind it. Use when a rep asks what to sell, pitch, recommend or bring up with a store. Every row says whether it is evidence based -- built on that account's own buying -- or only a suggestion, and those two must be said differently.
tools.subject: What should I sell them?
sample_questions: What should I sell Red Apple Market?
What should I talk to them about?
tools.answer_example: They are due for Soy Bean with Ginger Sauce, and Punjas Butter Snap Cookies are worth a mention. Want the detail on either?

tools.name: search_items
tools.description: Find PRODUCTS by what they are called. Use when someone asks whether we carry something, what brands or sizes there are, or what is in stock, and they have named the product rather than given a part number. Send two or three plain English words. Returns the item number, price, stock and whether it is on promotion. Nothing to do with customers or accounts.
tools.subject: What should I sell them?
sample_questions: Do we carry coconut milk?
What jasmine rice do we stock?
Anything on promotion in oyster sauce?
tools.answer_example: Several — DF Coconut Milk, Aroy D and Chaokoh. Want stock on one of them?

tools.name: lookup_item
tools.description: ONE product by its exact part number. Use when a caller reads out a number rather than a name. Returns stock on hand and shippable, price, case size, any live promotion and whether the item is discontinued. If they described the product in words instead, use search_items.
tools.subject: What should I sell them?
sample_questions: Is part 11050 in stock?
What's the promo on 11050?
tools.answer_example: Four thousand six hundred and eighty units of Golden Corn on Cob, as of last night.

tools.name: find_customer_by_name
tools.value_label: store or account being asked about
tools.description: Find a customer's account key from the name a caller said out loud. Use this FIRST whenever someone names a store rather than giving a key. Returns every active account matching those words with its city, post code and owning rep, because store names repeat -- many accounts share a name. Read the city and owner back and ask which one they mean before looking anything else up. Do not use this for products.
tools.subject: Who should I call?
sample_questions: How is Asian Market doing?
Look up Lee's Sandwiches
tools.answer_example: I found one Red Apple Market in Anchorage, owned by Tech Tov. Would you like their recent activity?

tools.name: lookup_account_status
tools.description: How ONE account is doing, by its customer key. Use for how an account is performing, when they last ordered, how long it has been, their recent order value, which days they accept deliveries and whether they need attention. If the caller gave a name instead of a key, run find_customer_by_name first. Do not use this for products or for a rep's own numbers.
tools.subject: Who should I call?
sample_questions: How is RED005 doing?
When did RED005 last order?
Which days does RED005 take deliveries?
tools.answer_example: Red Apple Market last ordered on the twenty-second, one day ago. Twenty-three orders recently, averaging about twenty-four thousand dollars.

tools.name: lookup_accounts_to_call
tools.description: Which of ONE REP's OWN accounts need a call, most urgent first. Requires the rep's name: these are their accounts, nobody else's, so never call this without knowing who you are speaking to -- ask first. Use when a rep asks who to call or visit, who has gone quiet, or which of their accounts need attention. Covers accounts seen within the last year. For one named store use lookup_account_status; for accounts near where they are standing use lookup_nearby_accounts.
tools.subject: Who should I call?
sample_questions: Which customers should I visit first today?
Which of my accounts have gone quiet?
tools.answer_example: Six of yours need a call. Tan Viet Oriental Food in Salina is the longest, three hundred and forty-three days, then Asian Market Grocery in Milwaukee.

tools.name: lookup_nearby_accounts
tools.value_label: account key they are standing at
tools.description: Other accounts NEAR a given account, closest and most urgent first, with how far away each is and why it needs attention. Use when a rep says they are at or near a store and asks who else is around, or who nearby has gone quiet. Needs the key of the account they are AT -- look the name up first if they gave one.
tools.subject: Who should I call?
sample_questions: I'm at Red Apple Market, who else is nearby?
Who near here has gone quiet?
tools.answer_example: Three within five kilometres. The closest that has gone quiet is a mile off and has not ordered in ninety days.

tbd._comment: Questions from the 9/8/2026 PDF that no built table answers. Shown in the web guide so a rep knows not to ask, rather than finding out mid-call. Each waits on a NAV table not yet exported to Databricks.
